title: Dark treacle toffee
subtitle: a rich, bittersweet toffee with deep treacle flavour
excerpt: Dark treacle toffee is the classic bonfire-night sweet: very firm, deeply flavoured, and nearly black from the black treacle. The syrup must be taken to the hard crack stage at 150°C or the toffee will be chewy rather than snapping. A buttered tin and a sugar thermometer are the two essentials.
sourceNotes: Dark treacle toffee is a traditional British bonfire night confectionery; early recipes appear in Mrs Beeton's Book of Household Management (1861, Project Gutenberg #10136) and other Victorian household manuals.

glossaryTerms.definition: A sugar cooking stage reached at 149 to 154°C, at which the syrup sets rigid and brittle when cooled.
A thick, dark, intensely flavoured syrup produced during sugar refining. Stronger and more bitter than molasses and much darker than golden syrup.

content.text: for its bitter, treacle depth and its nearly-black colour. The sugar syrup must reach
before it is poured: if poured too early, the result is a sticky, chewy toffee instead of the traditional snapping, brittle slab.
Toffee syrup reaches 150°C. Keep children away from the hob and have cold water nearby.
Butter a 20 cm square baking tin generously and line the base with baking parchment. Set it on a heatproof surface next to the hob.
Put all the ingredients into a medium heavy-based saucepan. Heat over a low-medium heat, stirring, until the sugar has dissolved and the butter has melted. Bring to the boil.
Clip the sugar thermometer to the side of the pan. Boil steadily without stirring until the temperature reaches 150°C. This takes about 12 to 15 minutes. The syrup will be very dark.
Remove from the heat the moment the thermometer reads 150°C. Pour immediately into the prepared tin. Do not scrape the pan.

Leave to cool at room temperature for at least 60 minutes until completely firm. Score into squares with a lightly oiled knife after 20 minutes while the toffee is still warm enough to cut without shattering.
Once fully cold and set, snap the toffee along the score lines. It should snap cleanly. Store in an airtight tin, each piece wrapped in a small square of waxed paper.

attrs.problem: Toffee is sticky and does not snap
attrs.avoid: Avoid pouring before the thermometer reaches 150°C.
attrs.fix: Use a calibrated thermometer and wait for the temperature to stabilise at 150°C before pouring.

attrs.avoid: Avoid stirring the syrup once it comes to the boil.
attrs.fix: Start with a fresh batch; crystallised toffee cannot be recovered. Stir only until the sugar dissolves, then stop.
